beats.text: Five Stoic lessons on handling criticism without it wrecking your day.
One. If the criticism is true, thank them. A free lesson just saved you from staying wrong.
Two. If it's false, it says more about them than about you. Let it stay theirs.
Three. You can't control opinions — only your character. Don't trade your peace for applause.
Four. Consider the source before the comment. Would you ask this person for directions?
Five. Be your own fair, honest judge first. Settle your own verdict, and others' words lose their grip.
The Stoic weighs criticism; he doesn't drown in it. Take the lesson, and leave the sting behind.
